Breadth is real (198 buyers ex-agent in the first two minutes, top-5 buyer share only 8.8%, sell-to-buy ratio near 1.0 at launch), and the coin is only 13.8% off its 30-minute high with a 900% 30-minute return. Pool depth of 333 SOL leaves room to exit a $20 ticket at a tolerable cost.

The honest counterweights: the curve is 100% bundle-funded with the top 3 holding 70%, and the sell volume in the last 15 minutes is nearly equal to buy volume, so the momentum is being absorbed by a large seller base. Base rates for alive coins 30-115 minutes post-graduation have been negative, and a 14% drawdown from a parabolic high is not a dip that most coins recover. Net flow is positive but thin relative to gross turnover. I see a demand case, but a weak one, and it does not clear the base rate.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a post-peak unwind by insiders and the launch bundle. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0 with 8 bundled buyers, and the completer holds 67.9% of the curve, so a small group controls most supply. The first two minutes after graduation had a launch bot present and a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.99, meaning nearly every SOL bought was matched by a SOL sold. The last 15 minutes show $5.7k SOL bought against $5.5k sold, with 1,588 sellers versus 2,013 buyers: distribution is already underway. The 13.8% drawdown from the 30-minute high, after a 9x run, suggests the peak is in. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a pool of only 333 SOL, a 20-40% reversal is likely to wipe out any bounce. Skip.
